title: Silas and the Radiators
premise: Lior Hartwell, a piano tuner who reads a building's history through the hum of its radiators, discovers a cache of undelivered letters hidden behind a wardrobe in a condemned apartment block — letters that reveal her late mentor Silas covered up a fatal accident decades ago to protect the neighborhood's beloved landlord. As demolition looms and the last bus route to the old quarter is rerouted, Lior must decide whether justice belongs to the courts, the dead, or the living who still need their stories. She delivers the letters publicly at the building's final tenant meeting, forcing a reckoning that costs her Silas's memory but wins her an unlikely found family among his victims' descendants. The novel ends with the wrecking ball suspended mid-air as the tenants win a stay of demolition — not saving the building, but buying time to tell the truth properly.
about_author: Theo Hartwell is the pen name of a former building superintendent who spent fifteen years listening to old houses complain. They write about the moral acoustics of ordinary places from a rented room above a laundromat.

chapters.title: The Hum Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Tuning a piano in the condemned Marlowe Building, she hears a radiator pulse out of rhythm with the rest of the house — a sound like a held breath. Establishes her gift for hearing buildings and her seven years of careful silence about Silas. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Letters Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Clearing a vacated unit, she pries loose a wardrobe panel and finds forty-one undelivered letters, all addressed by Silas in his unmistakable hand, none ever sent. The top one names a man who died in the 1989 boiler collapse. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past has been waiting in the walls.

chapters.title: What Silas Almost Said
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, intercut with one letter read aloud. She reconstructs Silas's habit of 'almost saying it' and realizes the letters were drafts of a confession he could never finish. Flashback texture: how he taught her to listen to radiators. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Landlord's Daughter
chapters.summary: Vera Okafor's POV. Vera, heir to the Marlowe estate and the neighborhood's benefactor, hosts a farewell tea for tenants. Lior attends, watching for cracks. Vera's warmth is real, but so is her control over every story told in the building. Emotional beat: charm as a form of power.

chapters.title: Bus Route 12
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Learning the last bus to the old quarter will be rerouted after demolition, she rides Route 12 end to end, tracing where each letter was meant to go. Two recipients are still alive. One slams the door; the other, an elderly welder named Amos, says only: 'I wondered when someone would find them.' Emotional beat: the door opening.

chapters.title: Amos Remembers Fire
chapters.summary: Amos's POV. In his kitchen, Amos describes the night of the collapse: Silas arrived before the ambulances left, carrying a toolbox and taking orders from young Vera's father. He never blamed Silas — 'a man can be a ladder or a wall.' Lior leaves shaken, understanding Silas chose to be a wall. Emotional beat: compassion complicating judgment.

chapters.title: Pressure in the Pipes
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera learns Lior has the letters and offers her money, then a role managing the estate archive — power dressed as generosity. Lior refuses, and Vera's mask slips just enough to show fear. Meanwhile tenants begin organizing against the demolition timeline. Emotional beat: corruption revealed not as villainy but as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Rerouting
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The city announces Route 12 ends Friday; demolition moves up. Lior realizes the truth will be buried with the building unless it surfaces now. She must choose between protecting Silas's memory and delivering what he couldn't. She photocopies all forty-one letters. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Last Tenant Meeting
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. At the final meeting in the Marlowe basement, amid radiator pipes groaning like a choir, Lior reads the letters aloud — including the one naming Vera's father. Vera stands, and instead of denying it, admits what she inherited and what she hid. The room fractures, then holds. Emotional beat: catharsis through unbearable honesty.

chapters.title: Stay of Demolition
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, mostly Lior's POV. The tenants win a temporary stay; the wrecking ball hangs idle. Lior mails the original letters to their addressees' families, finally doing what Silas couldn't. Amos helps her tune the lobby piano one last time. The building will fall eventually — but the story won't. Emotional beat: mourning and belonging arriving together.
